currentContext.business: SAMHI owns and asset-manages a diversified portfolio of branded hotels across India's major business and travel destinations, with the hotels themselves run by global operators under brands such as Marriott, Hyatt and Holiday Inn Express. Its revenue is entirely from accommodation and food service - rooms, food and beverage, banquets, spa, fitness centre, swimming pool and gym - serving individual leisure and business travellers, extended-stay residents, corporate groups, wedding parties and conference attendees. As of FY 2026 the platform ran 31 operating hotels with 4,899 rooms across 13 cities, spanning Mid-scale (12 hotels/1,729 rooms), Upper Mid-scale (14/2,047) and Upper Upscale & Upscale (5/1,123) segments, plus an asset-light leisure portfolio, with a further 7 hotels/1,669 rooms under development.

Asset-light leisure platform: Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy (proposed affiliation)

currentContext.expansion: FY 2026 was a pivotal expansion year in which SAMHI accelerated its transition into a diversified, institutional-grade hotel platform, adding four strategically significant hotel developments - two of them structured as capital-efficient variable leases. These were a ~162-room upper-upscale hotel in Sector 51, Noida, developed in partnership with Ingka Centres (part of the Ingka Group, which also owns IKEA Retail); a ~260-room mid-scale hotel secured on a long-term variable lease within the One Financial District development in Hyderabad; a Marriott-branded addition at Sriperumbudur, Chennai alongside the existing Fairfield (earlier proposed as an 86-room expansion of that Fairfield, now a 135-room hotel); and the Company's largest hotel to date, a ~700-room Westin and Fairfield by Marriott combination in Navi Mumbai that became possible after resolution of legacy issues relating to the asset. Four projects were completed during FY 2026 - the 133-room Holiday Inn Express rebranding at Knowledge Park, Greater Noida; the 113-room Holiday Inn Express new opening at Rajarhat, Kolkata; a 54-room expansion of the Sheraton at Gachibowli, Hyderabad; and a 56-room expansion of Holiday Inn Express, Whitefield, Bengaluru - while a 22-room expansion at Hyatt Regency, Nagar Road, Pune was in pre-opening. The under-development book stands at 7 hotels / 1,669 rooms with disclosed timelines: W, HITEC City, Hyderabad (170 rooms, new opening) and Courtyard by Marriott, Nagar Road, Pune (217 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton, part renovation in progress) in FY 2027; Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, Whitefield, Bengaluru (142 rooms, rebranding from Trinity) and Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, City Square, Jaipur (114 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton) in FY 2028; Westin, Whitefield, Bengaluru (220 rooms), the mid-scale hotel at Financial District, Hyderabad (260 rooms), the upper-upscale hotel at Sector 51, Noida (162 rooms) and Marriott, Sriperumbudur, Chennai (135 rooms) in FY 2030; and the two Navi Mumbai hotels, Westin (~350 rooms) and Fairfield by Marriott (~350 rooms), in FY 2031. Management describes six of these as transformative assets - W Hyderabad, Westin & Tribute Bangalore, the mid-scale hotel in Hyderabad, the upper-upscale hotel in Noida, the Marriott-Fairfield combination in Chennai and the Westin-Fairfield development in Navi Mumbai - with the potential to add ~Rs 10,000 mn of incremental revenue, a ~78% uplift over the current revenue base, as they come online. Funding is anchored on a commitment of ~Rs 22,000 mn of capex across the existing pipeline (including Navi Mumbai) over the next five years, supported by free cash flow (post-interest) of ~Rs 3,000 mn in FY 2026 versus ~Rs 900 mn at the time of the IPO, and by the strategic partnership with GIC, which provided a primary infusion of Rs 7,500 mn for a 35% minority stake in an upscale platform seeded with five hotels across Bengaluru and Pune and ~1,000 rooms (~Rs 6,000 mn received and invested during FY 2026, with ~Rs 1,500 mn committed for future funding of the Westin-Tribute Bangalore asset). Expansion is paired with disciplined asset recycling: the 142-room Hotel Caspia in New Delhi was divested in August 2025, part of a wider programme in which four non-core hotel divestments plus the GIC investment generated ~Rs 9,600 mn of proceeds, ~Rs 6,500 mn of which went to debt reduction and the balance to funding new acquisitions. Separately, the Company entered the asset-light experiential leisure segment by acquiring a 70% stake in RARE India (73 hotels / 1,015 rooms per the Board's Report; 75 hotels / ~1,046 rooms in the portfolio snapshot), intended to be brought under a distribution partnership with Marriott Bonvoy's Outdoor Collection.

risks.risk: Economic and industry risk - macroeconomic fluctuations and changing travel patterns
risks.note: Macroeconomic fluctuations or changing travel patterns may reduce occupancy levels and revenue growth. Management explicitly flags ongoing geopolitical instability in West Asia, which has rerouted international flights and raised travel costs, and can cause a selective slowdown in inbound Foreign Tourist Arrivals and alter established travel corridors. Mitigation is a diversified presence across major business hubs and leisure destinations (domestic leisure demand offsetting lulls in international corporate movement), dynamic pricing and value-added offerings tailored to safe-haven markets, and real-time tracking of travel trends through the SiD analytics platform.

risks.risk: Financial risk - capital structure imbalance and cash-flow constraints
risks.note: A capital structure imbalance or cash-flow constraint may affect financial stability and growth plans - material for a company carrying a large development pipeline. Mitigation is disciplined capital allocation, optimising operating costs through technology-led efficiencies, prioritising high-yield asset performance and actively managing portfolio mix for resilience.

risks.risk: Interest rate risk on a predominantly floating-rate borrowing book
risks.note: The Group's exposure to changes in market interest rates relates primarily to borrowings with floating interest rates, and the majority of the Group's borrowings are linked to floating rates, so borrowing costs adjust with the market. The Group evaluates market rates regularly to explore refinancing options, and discloses a 100 basis point cash-flow sensitivity on variable-rate instruments.

risks.risk: Liquidity and refinancing risk on a long-dated maturity profile
risks.note: Liquidity risk is the risk of difficulty in meeting obligations settled in cash. Management monitors rolling forecasts of liquidity, taking into consideration the Group's debt refinancing plans, undrawn committed borrowing facilities and covenant compliance; ultimate responsibility rests with the Board, which has established a liquidity risk management framework for short, medium and long-term funding requirements. The disclosed contractual maturity profile is weighted to the 2-5 year and beyond-5-year buckets.

risks.risk: Health and safety risk - operational lapses at hotel level
risks.note: Operational lapses may result in compliance exposure, liabilities or reputational impact. Mitigation is regular audits and real-time monitoring through centralised systems, application of global best practices in food, fire and hygiene standards, and continuous employee training on updated health protocols.

risks.risk: Regulatory and legal risk - labour, environmental, tax and data regulation
risks.note: Non-compliance with labour, environmental or data regulations may lead to penalties and operational disruption. Mitigation is automated compliance tracking tools, strengthened data protection measures across geographies and periodic internal audits with expert-led compliance reviews. The sector-wide GST rate change is a live example of regulatory change with a direct P&L effect - it impacted EBITDA growth by approximately 420 basis points in the short term.

risks.risk: Reputational risk - guest feedback and brand equity
risks.note: Negative publicity or poor guest feedback may impact brand equity and revenue, a particular exposure for a portfolio operated under third-party global brands. Mitigation is monitoring digital platforms and responding to feedback in real time, cross-functional resolution of guest concerns, continuous service training and transparent communication of sustainability initiatives.

risks.risk: Cost inflation, especially labour costs in metropolitan markets, and commodity/utility price volatility
risks.note: The Company explicitly frames lean staffing models, cluster management, multi-skilling and centralised procurement as protecting operating margins from rising labour costs in metropolitan markets and from volatile commodity prices for consumables, utilities and maintenance services - identifying both as ongoing margin pressures.

risks.risk: Credit risk on trade receivables from travel agents and corporate customers
risks.note: Credit sales without collateral are made principally to travel agents and corporate companies, with a credit policy analysing each new customer for creditworthiness; the Group states there are no significant concentrations of credit risk. Expected credit losses are provided under a provision matrix, with 100% loss allowance on receivables more than two years past due, and the loss-allowance provision on trade receivables increased over the year.

risks.risk: Currency risk on foreign-currency payables (management fees to global operators)
risks.note: Currency risk arises because future cash outflows on account of payables for management fees and other expenditure fluctuate with foreign exchange rates - a structural consequence of operating under global brand management agreements. Exposure is disclosed as USD trade payables, with a 5% movement sensitivity at March 31, 2026.

one-line thesis: SAMHI executes its first asset-light acquisition by taking a 70% stake in RARE India for ~INR 47cr, pivoting into the high-ADR experiential leisure segment via a strategic Marriott Bonvoy affiliation. While core Tier-1 business hotel strategy remains unchanged, this move creates a scalable, capital-efficient platform targeting INR 100cr revenue (from current INR 3cr) within 3-4 years by unlocking direct B2C bookings and pricing power for 67+ curated properties.
financial scorecard: Revenue: RARE target INR 3cr (current) vs INR 90-100cr (medium-term guidance); SAMHI consolidated FY26 guidance not updated on this call. EBITDA/Margin: RARE current EBITDA undisclosed (partnership firm); projected 60-70% RoCE post-transformation; margin profile expected to be moderate due to revenue share with Marriott distribution. themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SAMHI owns and asset-manages a diversified portfolio of branded hotels across India's major business and travel destinations, with the hotels themselves run by global operators under brands such as Marriott, Hyatt and Holiday Inn Express. Its revenue is entirely from accommodation and food service - rooms, food and beverage, banquets, spa, fitness centre, swimming pool and gym - serving individual leisure and business travellers, extended-stay residents, corporate groups, wedding parties and conference attendees. As of FY 2026 the platform ran 31 operating hotels with 4,899 rooms across 13 cities, spanning Mid-scale (12 hotels/1,729 rooms), Upper Mid-scale (14/2,047) and Upper Upscale & Upscale (5/1,123) segments, plus an asset-light leisure portfolio, with a further 7 hotels/1,669 rooms under development.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural upcycle in Indian hospitality driven by continued growth in office space absorption, infrastructure expansion and sustained corporate travel across key commercial markets.
- Supply-demand gap is the central driver: approximately 8,500 new branded rooms entered the market in FY 2026 taking total branded inventory to an estimated 175,000, a 5-6% pace of additions well below 8-9% demand growth in key commercial and leisure markets.
- Indian branded hotel sector entered FY 2026 with occupancy of 72-74% and ARR above Rs 8,200, both post-pandemic highs; ARR for premium/upper-upscale hotels ranged Rs 8,200-8,500 versus Rs 8,000-8,200 in the prior year, driving estimated RevPAR growth of ~8-10% YoY.
- ICRA projects industry revenue growth of 7-9% for FY 2027, with RevPAR maintaining a steady upward trajectory driven by domestic leisure travel, MICE demand, weddings and business travel; FY 2027 occupancy is projected at 73-75%, ARR at Rs 8,600-8,900 and RevPAR growth at 7-9%.
- MICE pipeline projected to grow from US$ 49.4 bn in FY 2024 to US$ 103.7 bn by FY 2030, supporting pricing power across the organised sector.
- Global Capability Centres - now exceeding 1,700 and concentrated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune - have emerged as a structural demand driver for urban hotels; GCCs accounted for nearly 38% of Grade A office leasing in 2025.
- Domestic-heavy demand profile buffers the portfolio: domestic travellers account for approximately 85% of the Company's room nights, insulating it from global volatility; India records over 3 bn domestic tourist visits.
- Diversification of demand sources - corporate travel, domestic leisure, weddings and pilgrimage each contributed independently, so the sector's revenue base is more resilient than at any point in the past decade; branded sector revenue grew an estimated 9-12% in FY 2026, a third consecutive year of double-digit or near-double-digit growth.
- Structural shift toward branded accommodation as consumers prioritise quality, standardisation and digital booking convenience.
- Operating leverage and cost rationalisation - large hotel entities reported operating margins of 34-36% in FY 2026, significantly above pre-pandemic averages; SAMHI's own profit before tax and exceptional items rose 89.3% on 12.3% revenue growth, reflecting embedded operating leverage.
- Redirected international travel away from the Middle East toward South Asia acted as a direct catalyst for Indian hospitality, boosting inbound tourism and hotel occupancy.
- Headwind: geopolitical volatility in early 2026 caused a 15-20% decline in inbound tourist traffic (PHDCCI), particularly leisure; airline rerouting and airspace restrictions raised international airfares and hit the FTA trajectory - domestic demand acted as the stabiliser.
- Headwind: global headline inflation projected to rise to 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027, with direct implications for hotel operating costs in F&B procurement, utilities, linen and general supplies, and for travel affordability and corporate travel budgets.
- Headwind flagged for FY 2026 performance: four one-time disruption events (India-Pakistan conflict, monsoon disruptions, an airline crisis and the Middle East conflict) cost ~Rs 440-520 mn of revenue, and a sector-wide GST rate change (12% with input tax credit to 5% without) compressed EBITDA growth by ~420 bps and cost ~Rs 180 mn.
- Management states that excluding these disruptions the underlying business would have delivered revenue growth of ~16-17% and EBITDA growth of ~19-20%.
- A stable and relatively accommodative rate environment supports demand by keeping retail borrowing manageable and preserving urban disposable income, while containing interest expense for hotel owners and supporting margin improvement and capital deployment flexibility.
- Aviation connectivity as a demand conduit: IATA projects Asia Pacific passenger traffic growth of 7.3% in 2026; India's domestic passenger traffic rose 1.4% YoY to 167.7 mn in FY 2026 and international traffic for Indian carriers grew 7.7% YoY.
- Industry-wide, operators are channelling expansion through asset-light management contracts and franchise arrangements rather than greenfield development, with a more active pipeline in Tier II/III cities.
- 1,669 rooms under development across 7 new-opening hotels in key metropolitan cities; the committed pipeline is expected to add revenue between FY 2027 and FY 2032.
- Six transformative assets in execution - W Hyderabad, Westin & Tribute Bangalore, a mid-scale hotel in Hyderabad, an upper-upscale hotel in Noida, a Marriott-Fairfield combination in Chennai and the Westin-Fairfield development in Navi Mumbai - with the potential to add ~Rs 10,000 mn of incremental revenue, a ~78% uplift over the current revenue base.
- FY 2027 deliveries: W, HITEC City, Hyderabad (170 rooms, new opening) and Courtyard by Marriott, Nagar Road, Pune (217 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton).
- FY 2028 deliveries: Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, Whitefield, Bengaluru (142 rooms, rebranding from Trinity) and Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, City Square, Jaipur (114 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton).
- FY 2030 deliveries: Westin, Whitefield, Bengaluru (220 rooms); Mid-scale Hotel, Financial District, Hyderabad (260 rooms); Upper Upscale Hotel, Sector 51, Noida (162 rooms); Marriott, Sriperumbudur, Chennai (135 rooms).
- FY 2031 deliveries: Westin, Navi Mumbai (~350 rooms) and Fairfield by Marriott, Navi Mumbai (~350 rooms) - together the largest hotel project in the Company's history at ~700 rooms.
- Completed in FY 2026: Holiday Inn Express Knowledge Park Greater Noida (133 rooms, rebranding), Holiday Inn Express Rajarhat Kolkata (113 rooms, new opening), Sheraton Hyderabad Gachibowli (54 rooms, expansion), Holiday Inn Express Whitefield Bengaluru (56 rooms, expansion); Hyatt Regency Pune Nagar Road (22-room expansion) was in pre-opening in FY 2026.
- Asset-light leisure pipeline: RARE India platform of 75 hotels / 1,046 rooms, currently under transition in collaboration with Marriott.
- Committed capex of ~Rs 22,000 mn across the existing pipeline (including Navi Mumbai) over the next five years.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2026 was a pivotal expansion year in which SAMHI accelerated its transition into a diversified, institutional-grade hotel platform, adding four strategically significant hotel developments - two of them structured as capital-efficient variable leases. These were a ~162-room upper-upscale hotel in Sector 51, Noida, developed in partnership with Ingka Centres (part of the Ingka Group, which also owns IKEA Retail); a ~260-room mid-scale hotel secured on a long-term variable lease within the One Financial District development in Hyderabad; a Marriott-branded addition at Sriperumbudur, Chennai alongside the existing Fairfield (earlier proposed as an 86-room expansion of that Fairfield, now a 135-room hotel); and the Company's largest hotel to date, a ~700-room Westin and Fairfield by Marriott combination in Navi Mumbai that became possible after resolution of legacy issues relating to the asset. Four projects were completed during FY 2026 - the 133-room Holiday Inn Express rebranding at Knowledge Park, Greater Noida; the 113-room Holiday Inn Express new opening at Rajarhat, Kolkata; a 54-room expansion of the Sheraton at Gachibowli, Hyderabad; and a 56-room expansion of Holiday Inn Express, Whitefield, Bengaluru - while a 22-room expansion at Hyatt Regency, Nagar Road, Pune was in pre-opening. The under-development book stands at 7 hotels / 1,669 rooms with disclosed timelines: W, HITEC City, Hyderabad (170 rooms, new opening) and Courtyard by Marriott, Nagar Road, Pune (217 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton, part renovation in progress) in FY 2027; Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, Whitefield, Bengaluru (142 rooms, rebranding from Trinity) and Tribute Portfolio by Marriott, City Square, Jaipur (114 rooms, rebranding from Four Points by Sheraton) in FY 2028; Westin, Whitefield, Bengaluru (220 rooms), the mid-scale hotel at Financial District, Hyderabad (260 rooms), the upper-upscale hotel at Sector 51, Noida (162 rooms) and Marriott, Sriperumbudur, Chennai (135 rooms) in FY 2030; and the two Navi Mumbai hotels, Westin (~350 rooms) and Fairfield by Marriott (~350 rooms), in FY 2031. Management describes six of these as transformative assets - W Hyderabad, Westin & Tribute Bangalore, the mid-scale hotel in Hyderabad, the upper-upscale hotel in Noida, the Marriott-Fairfield combination in Chennai and the Westin-Fairfield development in Navi Mumbai - with the potential to add ~Rs 10,000 mn of incremental revenue, a ~78% uplift over the current revenue base, as they come online. Funding is anchored on a commitment of ~Rs 22,000 mn of capex across the existing pipeline (including Navi Mumbai) over the next five years, supported by free cash flow (post-interest) of ~Rs 3,000 mn in FY 2026 versus ~Rs 900 mn at the time of the IPO, and by the strategic partnership with GIC, which provided a primary infusion of Rs 7,500 mn for a 35% minority stake in an upscale platform seeded with five hotels across Bengaluru and Pune and ~1,000 rooms (~Rs 6,000 mn received and invested during FY 2026, with ~Rs 1,500 mn committed for future funding of the Westin-Tribute Bangalore asset). Expansion is paired with disciplined asset recycling: the 142-room Hotel Caspia in New Delhi was divested in August 2025, part of a wider programme in which four non-core hotel divestments plus the GIC investment generated ~Rs 9,600 mn of proceeds, ~Rs 6,500 mn of which went to debt reduction and the balance to funding new acquisitions. Separately, the Company entered the asset-light experiential leisure segment by acquiring a 70% stake in RARE India (73 hotels / 1,015 rooms per the Board's Report; 75 hotels / ~1,046 rooms in the portfolio snapshot), intended to be brought under a distribution partnership with Marriott Bonvoy's Outdoor Collection.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Ability to work with institutional capital - stated explicitly under 'What Sets Us Apart' and evidenced by the GIC partnership, under which ~Rs 7,500 mn was committed and ~Rs 6,000 mn received during FY 2026 for a 35% minority stake in a ~1,000-room platform
- Acquisition and turnaround experience - a stated differentiator; strategy is to 'acquire at a discount to replacement cost, manage actively, and scale with discipline'
- Dominant share with leading operators - long-standing partnerships with leading global hospitality brands (Marriott, Hyatt, IHG/Holiday Inn Express), giving access to their distribution and brand systems
- Analytical, data-driven approach - proprietary technology platform 'SiD' integrating operational, financial and asset-level intelligence, enabling faster decision-making, sharper underwriting and more efficient post-acquisition integration
- Scale and diversification across segments (Mid-scale to Upper Upscale) and 13 cities, with carefully selected micro-markets and diversified demand drivers, supporting portfolio resilience
- Domestic-heavy demand profile - domestic travellers are ~85% of room nights, buffering the portfolio against global volatility
- Strengthened balance sheet and financing quality - effective interest rate reduced to 7.9%, ~290 bps lower than at the time of IPO, and credit rating upgraded to A+ (CARE/ICRA) during FY 2026
- Capital-efficient growth structures - long-term variable lease models (Noida with Ingka Centres, Hyderabad Financial District) and asset-light platform ownership (RARE India) allow expansion while preserving capital
- Clustered operating model and shared service capabilities allowing efficient scaling while maintaining operational discipline

risks.body: Integration risk: Potential conflicts with existing niche affiliations (e.g., Mr & Mrs Smith, SLH) for some properties (estimated single-digit %); Seasonality: Leisure segment volatility and geopolitical sensitivity; Execution: Delay in B2C tech transition or Marriott integration could defer revenue ramp; Valuation: High multiple on current earnings (INR 3cr revenue) relies entirely on successful transformation.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The acquisition is valued at ~INR 4.5 lakh per room, which management argues is cheap compared to greenfield startup valuations; the deal secures access to a 23-year-old curated community of owners that cannot be replicated by capital alone; SAMHI gains a proprietary leisure data set to de-risk future potential leisure asset bets without committing capital now.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Three-pillar core strategy, unchanged: acquire hotel assets at a discount to replacement cost, manage them actively, and scale with discipline.
- Focus on high-density, demand-resilient markets - a targeted presence in high-potential micro-markets across India's major business and travel destinations, aligned with the country's economic growth centres.
- Deepen partnerships with leading global hotel brands (Marriott, Hyatt, IHG) and use data-driven insights to enhance portfolio performance.
- Grow through capital-efficient structures - long-term variable leases (Sector 51 Noida with Ingka Centres; …

| Limited exposure to high-growth experiential leisure segment; high capital intensity of traditional hotel expansion | SAMHI Hotels Limited | beneficiary | High | Acquires scalable leisure platform with INR 100cr revenue potential for only INR 47cr; leverages existing Marriott relationship for distribution without heavy capex; diversifies revenue mix while maintaining core focus. |
| Independent boutique hotels lack global distribution reach and tech infrastructure to capture high-value direct bookings | RARE India Portfolio Owners | beneficiary | High | Gain access to Marriott Bonvoy's global distribution network and SAMHI's revenue management expertise; expected uplift in occupancy (from 35-45%) and ADR through dynamic pricing enablement. |
| Need to expand 'Outdoor Collection' inventory in India with authentic, non-standardized assets without heavy investment | Marriott International | beneficiary | Med | Instantly acquires curated portfolio of 67+ unique properties fitting the 'Outdoor Collection' niche without asset ownership risk; strengthens loyalty program offerings in experiential travel segment. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [GST regime change] "Shift from 12% with ITC to 5% without input credit compressed reported EBITDA growth by ~₹92mn for the quarter", spread as ~₹82mn across operating cost heads plus ~₹10mn in corporate G&A; management expects margins to recover as new openings skew upscale.
- [Marriott partnership — pending] Of RARE's 75 hotels, "40+ hotels have agreed to be on Marriott Outdoor Collection"; 15 pilot properties are shortlisted for integration in H2FY27, with RARE positioned to become the exclusive 'Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy' platform across India, Nepal and Bhutan. The deck repeatedly calls this partnership "pending"/"under transition".
- [Approval delay] Hyatt Regency Pune: "22 apartments have been fully completed; delay in approvals causing loss of revenue in a strong market" — listed by the company itself under "Misses & headwinds".
- [Geopolitical headwind] Q1FY27 performance was delivered "despite headwinds faced due to middle east conflict"; the deck's AAI data shows Q1FY27 air passengers roughly flat (+0.1% YoY) with Hyderabad −12.1%, Chennai −9.9% and Goa −5.2%, attributed to "large dependence on gulf carriers for international traffic".
- [Portfolio churn] Recent portfolio changes referenced in same-store footnotes: Trinity acquired Oct'24, HIEX Greater Noida reopened Dec'24, HIEX Kolkata opened May'25, Four Points by Sheraton Chennai OMR sold Feb'25 and Caspia Delhi sold and treated as a discontinued operation (FY25 financials restated on that account).
